newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Demand appears to be waning.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds - Demand appears to be waning.

text.p: Demand for millfeeds appeared to be waning in several locations as lush pastures and availability of other feed ingredients has lessened the need for millfeeds, dealers said.
The benchmark Kansas City rail market was steady to lower, offered at $80.00 per ton, down $4.00 from Friday.
"They (feedmixers) just don't need it right now," said a Kansas City dealer.
Dealers said feed sales have slipped because spring pastures have lessened the demand for feed and farmers were buying less as they concentrated on planting corn and soybeans.

A Carolina dealer said an increase in feed production during the weekend had millfeed dealers raising offers about $7.00 per ton to $91.00. However, he said the higher prices should quickly cool demand.
"The buyers will resist (the higher prices) and prices will drop," he said.
Buffalo sources said a slight increase in flour mill production had ample supplies available in that market, which weighed slightly on offers.
